:: J U D G M E N T :

Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/ for the death of Kumar H.R. @ Punith in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 29.06.2018, at about 7.30 p.m., Kumar H.R. @ Punith was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN4454 from Nuggehalli to his village Hulikere.

When Kumar H.R., @ Punith was moving near M.M.L. Mains office, one dog came infront of the motor cycle to cross the road, for which all of a sudden Kumar H.R., @ Punith lost control the motor cycle and fell down and he sustained injuries.

Immediately someone informed the accident to the petitioners and Kumar H.R., @ Punith was shifted to Hassan Government Hospital, wherein he was taken treatment as an Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
2 inpatient for two days
. The doctors have advised him to take higher treatment at NIMHANS Hospital.
For which Kumar H.R., @ Punith was shifted to Victoria Hospital, inspite of treatment, he has not recovered and succumbed to injuries on 02.07.2018 at about 1.00 a.m.
After postmortem at Victoria Hospital, dead body of the deceased Kumar H.R., @ Punith, dead body was handed over to petitioners.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and cremation of deceased.
Deceased was aged about 30 years at the time of his death, he was doing agriculture and milk vending and earning Rs.4,000/ per month.
He has contributed his entire earnings towards maintenance of family.
The deceased was the only earning member in the family and the petitioners are totally depending on his earning.
The petitioners have lost their only son.
The Nuggehalli Police have registered a case in Crime No.196/2018 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1st respondent is the RC owner of aforesaid motor cycle and the 2nd respondent is the insurer.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
With these averments petitioners prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

In so for as the 1 st respondent is concerned, being the previous R.C.
owner of the vehicle appeared through his counsel, but did not filed written statement.
The 2nd respondent being the present R.C. owner of the vehicle remained absent, hence he was placed Ex parte.

4. The written statement averments of 3rd respondent is as hereunder:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent has denied entire allegations made in the petition.

The specific contention of the 3rd respondent is that, as per the police documents, the deceased himself was riding the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN4454 and same was obtained from the 2nd respondent.
Once the deceased has taken the vehicle from the owner and it was riding, he will stepped into the shoes of the owner, he himself become the owner and he cannot be treated as a third party.
Further contended that, no other vehicle was involved in the accident and the charge sheet was filed against the deceased himself for rash or negligent riding.
Further contended that, the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 05HN 4454 is not insured with this respondent and the petitioners have not furnished any policy particulars.
The deceased was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident.
The 3rd respondent has denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased, age, occupation and income of deceased.
It is contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has not informed the accident and not furnished the particulars of policy as contemplated under Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act.

There is no nexus between the accident and injuries sustained by the deceased, only to fetch compensation, the petitioners have created the documents in collusion with the police, hence there is non compliance of Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.

With these averments, the 3rd Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
3 respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has recast the Issues, the recasted issues are as hereunder:

:: ISSUES ::
1.
Whether petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased Kumar H.R. @ Punith and were dependent on him?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased namely Kumar H.R. @ Punith succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.06.2018 at about 7.30 p.m., near M.M.L. Office opposite, when he was riding a vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN 4454?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.2 examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Learned counsel for Respondent No.3 has crossexamined P.W.1.
Respondent No.3 examined its Administrative Officer as R.W.1 and marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
R.W.1 has not been cross examined from the side of petitioners.
7. Heard the arguments of both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of the Tribunal to the above referred issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following.

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:
According to the petitioners, 1st petitioner is the mother and 2nd petitioner is the father of deceased.
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
In order to answer this aspect, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.9 are relevant.
On careful perusal of these documents, it appears to this Court that, as per Ex.P.2, the 2nd petitioner has lodged the complaint.
In the complaint, there is a recital that, deceased is the son of 2 nd petitioner.
Likewise, in Ex.P.9, i.e., Postmortem examination report, wherein also the deceased is shown as son of Rangaswamy i.e., the 2nd petitioner.

During the course of cross examination of Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
4 P.W.1, the P.W.1 has expressed his ignorance regarding filing of charge sheet against his son.
Further learned counsel for respondent No.3 suggested that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the son of P.W.1.
Therefore, it can be inferred that, the petitioners are the parents of deceased and they are the dependents of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE No.2:

The case of the petitioners is that, on 29.06.2018 at about 7.30 p.m., while the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN4454 near M.M.L. Mains Office,
Hulikere village, one dog suddenly came infront of the said vehicle.
Due to said impact, deceased lost control over the motor cycle and feel down and sustained severe injuries.
Further case of the petitioners is that, the deceased has taken treatment as an inpatient for two days at Government Hospital, Hassan.

As per the advise of doctors, he was shifted to Victoria Hospital for higher treatment, but he succumbed to injuries on 02.07.2018 at about 1.00 a.m.
10.
According to the respondent No.3, on the date of accident, deceased himself was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN4454 and he lost control over the motor cycle and fell down on the Gutter.
Due to said impact he sustained grievous injuries on his head and succumbed to the injuries on 02.07.2018.
The charge sheet was also filed against the deceased himself and he is the Tort feasor.
Hence, the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.163A is not maintainable.
11. In order to prove the claim of petitioners, petitioner No.2 was examined as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
P.W.1 also produced as many as 10 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
The 2nd respondent has examined its Administrative Officer namely Prashanth N.G., as R.W.1.
R.W.1 has reiterated the written statement averments by filing affidavit evidence and Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 were marked.
R.W.1 has not been crossexamined from the side of petitioners.
12. Now itself it is appropriate to see the documents marked at Ex.PSeries and Ex.RSeries.
Ex.PSeries and Ex.RSeries.

Ex.P.9 is the true copy of P.M. Report.
Ex.P.10 is the true copy of charge sheet.
Ex.R.1 is the Authorization letter of R.W.1.

Ex.R.2 is the insurance policy of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN 4454.
13.
The petitioners have filed this petition u/Sec.163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Under these circumstances the petitioners need not prove the rash or negligence but it is sufficient that they prove the occurrence of the accident by involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the deceased.

5 14.

Further, it is pertinent to note that in a petition filed under Section 163A of MV Act, the question to be considered by the Tribunal is the involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide question of the entitlement for compensation.

Section 163A of the Act reads as under;
"not withstanding anything contained in this act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in case of death or permanent disablement due to the accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the second schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim as the case may be".

Again, it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in 'United India Insurance Vs. Sunil Kumar and Another' wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under;
"........in a proceedings under Section 163A of IMV Act it is not open for the insurer to raise any defence or plea of negligence on the part of the victim".

entities.text: United India Insurance Vs. Sunil Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in para No.8 of the said judgment, it is clearly observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that, "... it is clear that grant of compensation under Section 163A of the Act on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of final award and the adjudication there under is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle/s involved in the accident.
This is made explicit by Section 163(a)(2).

Though the aforesaid Section of the act does Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
6 not specifically exclude the possible defence of insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated under Section 140(4)

entities.text: Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , to permit such defence to be introduced by the insurer and or to understand the provision of Section 163A of the act to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163A of the act, namely final compensation with a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situation where the claims of the compensation on the basis of the fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

In fact, to understand the Section 163A of the act to permit the insurer to raise the defense of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under section 163A of the act at par with the proceedings under section 166 of the act which would not only be self contradictory, but also defeat the very legislative intention."

19. In view of above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident.

According to the petitioners, deceased was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN4454 from Nuggehalli to his village, at which point of time, one dog was coming cross of deceased motor cycle and all of a sudden son of petitioners lost control, met with an accident and succumbed to the fatal injuries.

Thereafter,
20.
It is relevant to note that, police have filed the charge sheet against the deceased.
Let this Tribunal put it simply, the police have filed the abated charge sheet.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, the son of petitioners died in an accident.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3: According to the respondent No.3, the deceased himself riding the vehicle by obtaining the same from 2 nd respondent.
Once he has taken from the owner and riding, he will stepped into the shoes of owner.
Under such circumstances, he will not become third party.
In support of his contentions, he has relied on the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

The decisions relied by the counsel for the respondent No.3 are as under:
1. (2009) 13 SCC 710, between Ningamma and Another Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited.
2. 2020 (2) SCC 550, between Ramkhiladi and Another VS.

sentences.text:
It is true that, in a claim under Section 163A of the Act, there is no need for the claimants to plead or Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
7 establish the negligence and/or that the death in respect of which the claim petition is sought to be established was due to wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle concerned.
It is also true that the claim petition under Section 163A of the Act is based on the principle of nofault liability.

However, at the same time, the deceased has to be a third party and cannot maintain a claim under Section 163A of the Act against the owner/insurer of the vehicle which is borrowed by him as he will be in the shoes of the owner and he cannot maintain a claim under Sec.163A of the Act against the owner and insurer of the vehicle bearing Registration No.RJ 02 SA 7811.
In the present case, the parties are governed by the contract of insurance and under the contract of insurance the liability of the insurance company would be qua third party only.
In the present case as observed hereinabove, the deceased cannot be said to be a third party with respect to the insured vehicle bearing Registration No.RJ 02 SA 7811.
There cannot be any dispute that the liability of the insurance company would be as per the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

As held by this Court in Dhanraj, an insurance policy covers the liability incurred by the insurer in respect of death of or bodily injury to any person (including an owner of the goods or his authorised representative) carried in the vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle.
In the said decision, it is further held by this Court that Section 147 does not require an insurance company to assume risk for death or bodily injury to the owner of the vehicle.

9.6. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, in the present case, as the claim under Section 163A of the Act was made only against the owner and insurance company of the vehicle which was being driven by the deceased himself as borrower of the vehicle from the owner of the vehicle and he would be in the shoes of the owner

, the High Court has rightly observed and held that such a claim was not maintainable and the claimants ought to have joined and/or ought to have made the claim under Section 163A of the Act against the driver, owner and/or the insurance company of the offending vehicle i.e., RJ 29 2M 9223 being a third party to the said vehicle.

9.7. Now, so far as the reliance placed upon by the learned advocate for the claimants on the decision of this Court in Naveen Kumar, on considering the issue involved in that decision, we are of the opinion that the said decision shall not be applicable to the fact of the case on hand and/or the same shall not be of any assistance to the claimants.

In that case, the issue was as to who could be said to be the registered owner of the vehicle and the liability of the owner who sold the vehicle, but his name continued to be as the owner with the registering authority.
To that, it was held that, the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered is the owner of the vehicle for the purpose of the Act.
9.8. However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the ownerdriver is entitled to a sum of Rs 1 lakh.

Therefore, the deceased, as observed hereinabove,
who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

However, it is the case on behalf of the original claimants that there is an amendment to the 2nd Schedule and a fixed amount of Rs. 5 lakh has been specified in case of death and therefore the claimants hall be entitled to Rs 5 lakh.
The same cannot be accepted.

In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the judgment and award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned judgment and order has been passed by the High Court in 1052018 i.e., much prior to the amendment in the 2nd schedule.

In the facts and circumstance of the present case, the claimants shall not be entitled to the benefit for the Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
8 amendment to the 2nd schedule.
At the same time, as observed hereinabove, the claimants shall be entitled to Rs 1 lakh as per the terms of the contract of insurance, the driver being in the shoes of the owner of the vehicle.

9.9. Now, so far as the submission made on behalf of of the claimants that in a claim under Section 163A of the Act mere use of the vehicle is enough and despite the compensation claimed by the heirs of the owner of the motorcycle which was involved in the accident resulting in his death, the claim under Section 163A of the Act would be maintainable is concerned, in view of decision of this Court in Rajni Devi, the aforesaid cannot be accepted.

In Rajni Devi, it has been specifically observed and held that the provisions of Section 163A of the Act cannot be said to have any application with regard to an accident wherein the owner of the motor vehicle himself is involved.

After considering the decisions of this Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V. Jhuma Saha;
Dhanraj; National Insurance Co. Ltd., V. Laxmi Narain Dhut and Premkumari V. Prahlad Dev, it is ultimately concluded by this Court that the liability under Section 163A of the Act is on the owner of the vehicle as a person cannot be both, a claimant as also a recipient and therefore, the heirs of the owner could not have maintained the claim in terms of Section 163A of the Act.

sentences.text: It is further observed that, for the said purpose, only the terms of the contract of insurance could be taken recourse to.
In the recent decision of this Court in Ashalata Bhowmik, it is specifically held by this Court that the parties shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

Therefore, as per the contract of insurance, the insurance company shall be liable to pay the compensation to a third party and not to the owner, except to the extent of Rs.1 lakh as observed hereinabove.

10. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, the present appeal is partly allowed to the aforesaid extend and it is observed and held that the original claimants shall be entitled to a sum of Rs 1 lakh only with interest @ 7.5 per cent per annum from the date of the claim petition till realisation.
23. In the instant case, the 3rd respondent has produced policy and the same has been marked as Ex.R.2.
On careful perusal of Ex.R.2, as on the date of accident, the policy was in force.
Further, it is crystal clear that, the insurance company had collected the premium of Rs.50/ to cover the risk of personal accident of owner driver to the maximum limit of Rs.1,00,000/.

In view of the ratio laid down in the above decision coupled with ratio laid down in the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A.No.101420/2019 (M.V.) between Smt. Pushpalatha and Others Vs.
Sharanabasappa and Another, the petitioners at the most entitled for compensation as per terms of contract only under personal accident cover.

Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.3 in the Partly Affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.4:.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:

Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.

Respondent No.3 being insurer of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. :

On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioners are entitled for 50% each with interest.
Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.

Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/ for the death of Kumar H.R. @ Punith in the road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The deceased was the only earning member in the family and the petitioners are totally depending on his earning.
The petitioners have lost their only son.
The Nuggehalli Police have registered a case in Crime No.196/2018 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1st respondent is the RC owner of aforesaid motor cycle and the 2nd respondent is the insurer.
The deceased was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has not informed the accident and not furnished the particulars of policy as contemplated under Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act.
There is no nexus between the accident and injuries sustained by the deceased, only to fetch compensation, the petitioners have created the documents in collusion with the police, hence there is non compliance of Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
The decisions relied by the counsel for the respondent No.3 are as under:
1. (2009) 13 SCC 710, between Ningamma and Another Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited.
2. 2020 (2) SCC 550, between Ramkhiladi and Another VS.
United
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: ISSUES ::
1.
Whether petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased Kumar H.R. @ Punith and were dependent on him?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased namely Kumar H.R. @ Punith succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.06.2018 at about 7.30 p.m., near M.M.L. Office opposite, when he was riding a vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05HN 4454?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to said impact he sustained grievous injuries on his head and succumbed to the injuries on 02.07.2018.
The petitioners have filed this petition u/Sec.163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Renukamma vs Dental Art Lab on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49269289/
5 14.
Further, it is pertinent to note that in a petition filed under Section 163A of MV Act, the question to be considered by the Tribunal is the involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide question of the entitlement for compensation.
Section 163A of the Act reads as under;
"not withstanding anything contained in this act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in case of death or permanent disablement due to the accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the second schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim as the case may be".
19. In view of above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident.

However, at the same time, the deceased has to be a third party and cannot maintain a claim under Section 163A of the Act against the owner/insurer of the vehicle which is borrowed by him as he will be in the shoes of the owner and he cannot maintain a claim under Sec.163A of the Act against the owner and insurer of the vehicle bearing Registration No.RJ 02 SA 7811.
In the present case, the parties are governed by the contract of insurance and under the contract of insurance the liability of the insurance company would be qua third party only.
There cannot be any dispute that the liability of the insurance company would be as per the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.
In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the judgment and award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned judgment and order has been passed by the High Court in 1052018 i.e., much prior to the amendment in the 2nd schedule.
23. In the instant case, the 3rd respondent has produced policy and the same has been marked as Ex.R.2.
On careful perusal of Ex.R.2, as on the date of accident, the policy was in force.
Further, it is crystal clear that, the insurance company had collected the premium of Rs.50/ to cover the risk of personal accident of owner driver to the maximum limit of Rs.1,00,000/.

24. ISSUE No.4:.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.3 being insurer of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. :
APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioners are entitled for 50% each with interest.
Scheme of investment is dispensed with as amount awarded is too meager.
